title: HOMECOMING PARADE TONIGHT
full_story:
The Flora High School Homecoming Parade will be held tonight, beginning at 7:30 pm through downtown Flora.  The parade will start at the Depot with line up at 7, and end at the corner of North Avenue and Mill Street.  The Flora Fire Department will be selling pork burgers, chips, and water at the fire department, starting at 5 pm, cost is by donation.  Class Competitions will then be held on Dancey Field at 8 with the bonfire to follow.

Today is Color War Day, Seniors will wear black, Juniors will wear yellow, Sophomores will wear Red, and Freshmen will wear Green.  Faculty will be dressed in Blue.  Tomorrow will be Dolly Parton Day and Pink Out Day. and Friday will be Crazy Orange and Blue Day.  Friday night, at 7 pm will be the Homecoming Football game at Dancey Field, against the Eldorado Eagles with the Homecoming court announced during half time of the game.

The student body has chosen the Queen candidates of Myra Sloan, Marli Myers, Qynlin Brown, Danica Conklin and Rosalyn Stanford.  King Candidates are Guy Arnold, Rylan Billingsly, Kehlin Crawford, Brennan O’Donnell, and Kormik Massie.  The Junior Class attendants are Morgan Irmen, Mylea Jones, Kennedy Zimmerman, Tyler Earnst, Braxton Oestrich, and Ashton Williams.  The Sophomores Class attendants are Vayda Kohn and Carson Smith.  The Freshmen Class Attendants are Halle Patridge and Sawyer Murbarger.

The coronation of the King and Queen will be held Saturday night, in the FHS Gym.  Dance opens at 7 for students, parents are welcome to enter at 7:15, coronation begins at 7:30 and dance is from 8 to 10 pm.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross is appealing for blood and platelet donors of all blood types to schedule donation appointments this fall.  The organization provides more than 6.5 million blood products to hospitals nationwide each year.

The call for donations aligns with National Preparedness Month in September.  Red Cross officials stated that maintaining a sufficient blood supply is necessary for disaster response, including home fires and natural disasters.

There will be a Blood Drive on Friday in the conference room of the Clay County Health Department from 1 to 5 pm.  Donors who give blood or platelets before October 18th will receive a $15 e-gift card to a merchant of their choice.

To be eligible to donate, individuals must be at least 17 years old, or 16 with parental consent, where permitted by state law and weigh at least 110 pounds while in generally good health.  High school students and other donors 18 years of age and younger must also meet specific height and weight requirements.  Donors must present a blood donor card, driver’s license or two other forms of identification at check-in.

Appointments can be made using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or by enabling the Blood Donor Skill on Alexa Echo devices.  Donors can use RapidPass online on the day of their appointment to complete pre-donation reading and health history questionnaires before arriving.

The next Blood Drive in the area will be on Tuesday, October 6th from Noon to 6 pm at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church.

title: MITIGATION PLANNING COMMITTEE MEETING
full_story:
Mitigation projects and activities that can reduce injuries and fatalities while maintaining vital services for Clay County residents will be the main topic of discussion at the upcoming Clay County Hazard Mitigation Planning Committee meeting.  The meeting will be held at the Clay County Health Department, 601 E. 12th Street, in Flora, at 1 pm on Wednesday, October 7th.

The Committee began work in January to update the county’s Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan.  This plan details the past severe weather events that have impacted the County and identifies mitigation projects and activities that can be taken before an event occurs to protect residents and critical services and infrastructure.

“Obtaining FEMA’s approval of our updated Plan will make all of the participants eligible to apply for federal grant money for mitigation projects and activities,” said Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency Coordinator, Steve Lewis.

Building community safe rooms, acquiring flood prone properties, resolving drainage issues, retrofitting critical infrastructure to better withstand hazard events, installing back-up power supplies, and developing public information materials are a few of the mitigation projects more commonly proposed in Illinois.

Projects identified by Committee members at this meeting will become part of the County’s updated Plan.  While the committee has provided input on portions of the Plan, the Plan will be presented in full for public review and comment before it is submitted to the state and federal government for approval.

“A public forum will be conducted after the first of the year for interested persons to review the Plan update and ask questions of Committee Members.  A two-week public comment period will be held following the public forum to accommodate interested residents who are unable to attend.  We want to make sure that anybody who is interested has an opportunity to review and comment on the draft Plan update,” added Lewis.

Interested persons can submit questions and comments to the Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency office.

title: COMPUTERS FOR BEGINNERS CLASSES
full_story:
Frontier Community College will offer two Computers for Beginners classes in October for individuals interested in developing their basic computer skills and becoming more comfortable using technology.

The first class will be held on October 6th from 11:30 am to 4:30 pm, followed by a second opportunity on October 22nd from noon to 4 pm.  Both classes will take place in Room 32 of Workforce Development Center on Frontier Community College’s campus.

Computers for Beginners is designed to provide participants with an opportunity to develop their computer skills in an accessible learning environment.  Whether participants have limited experience with computers or simply want to become more confident with technology, the classes provide an opportunity to strengthen their knowledge and skills.

Those interested in attending can register by contacting KaRissa Miller at 618-847-9276 or by email at [email protected].  Interested people can also register by scanning the QR code on flyers or on the college Facebook page.

title: CROP REPORT
full_story:
While some combines are just getting started on grain harvest, other farmers are rolling out equipment to seed winter wheat.  In its latest crop progress and condition report Monday, USDA estimated 3% of the state’s wheat is planted with 1% emerged.  Corn and soybean harvest progress is ahead of average, driven by a strong start in southern Illinois.

According to the USDA there were 5.8 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending September 20th.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 11% very short, 25% short, 55% adequate and 9% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 11% very short, 26% short, 58% adequate, and 5% surplus.

Corn dented reached 94%, compared to the 5-year average of 92%.  Corn mature reached 69%, compared to the 5-year average of 63%. Corn harvested reached 16% compared to the 5-year average of 9%.  Corn condition was rated 5% very poor, 9% poor, 29% fair, 43% good, and 14% excellent.

Soybeans dropping leaves reached 67%, compared to the 5-year average of 65%.  Soybeans harvested reached 13%, compared to the 5-year average of 5%.  Soybeans condition was rated 5% very poor, 8% poor, 30% fair, 44% good, and 13% excellent.

Winter Wheat planted is now at 3% compared to the 5-year average of 4%.

title: FMH MEMORIAL BRICKS
full_story:
The Fairfield Memorial Hospital Foundation is inviting community members, families, businesses and supporters to become a permanent part of the hospital’s history through the purchase of an engraved commemorative brick.

For $500 per brick, individuals can create a personalized tribute honoring a loved one, celebrating a healthcare hero, recognizing a family or business, memorializing someone special, or simply leaving their own lasting legacy at Fairfield Memorial Hospital.

Each engraved brick will become a permanent part of the hospital grounds, creating a meaningful tribute that can be enjoyed by generations to come.

The commemorative brick program offers supporters an opportunity to be part of Fairfield Memorial Hospital’s history while helping the Hospital Foundation continue its mission of supporting the hospital and its patients.

Each brick can be personalized with up to three lines of text, with 16 characters per line, including spaces.  Bricks are available for $500 each.

For more information about purchasing a commemorative brick, contact Nathan Gentz, Foundation Director, at 618-847-8391 or [email protected].

title: FEE DROPPED
full_story:
Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias eliminated an additional fee for notaries who provide electronic notarization services, making it easier and more affordable for Illinoisans to have documents notarized.

As a result, Illinois notaries public can become commissioned electronic notaries without paying the additional $25 commission fee.  The waiver, which took effect July 27th, is already helping expand access to electronic notarization.  As of Sept. 9th, 137 applications for both Notary Public and Electronic Notary commissions had been submitted, resulting in nearly $3,500 in waived fees.

Giannoulias launched Illinois’ Electronic Notary System in April 2024, allowing Illinoisans to have documents notarized electronically without having to meet with a notary in person.  E-notary allows customers and notaries to sign documents electronically and attach the notarial certificate and seal electronically.  There are currently 3,369 Illinois notaries who are also commissioned electronic notaries.

The Secretary of State’s office has also streamlined the notary application process.  Since August 2024, Illinoisans have been able to apply online to become notaries public and current notaries can renew their registrations online, eliminating paper-based applications and reducing processing times.

Illinoisans looking for a notary who provides electronic notarization can use the Secretary of State’s notary search at apps.ilsos.gov/notarysearch.  Customers will need a computer, smartphone or other device that supports audio-video communication and a valid form of identification to complete an electronic notarization.

Electronic notarial acts remain subject to fees established by state law, with a maximum fee of $25.

title: VISITORS CENTER TO CLOSE
full_story:
Illinois’ eight state-run visitor information centers, located within rest areas at interstates around the state, will be closing by the end of the month.

“The role of the State’s visitor information centers has evolved significantly over the past couple of decades as the ways visitors plan and access travel information have changed,” the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity told Capitol News Illinois in a statement.  “For example, the centers used to provided services such as booking hotel rooms for tourists, while that is no longer a need of many travelers.”

The closures were independent of financial pressures, according to the agency.  Operating the centers cost the state approximately $1.6 million per year.

The rest areas where the centers are located will continue operating, and other services will be uninterrupted, the department added.  The closures do not extend to independently operated visitor information centers by local governments or tourism organizations.

The state did not publicly announce the news but confirmed the closures to Capitol News Illinois when asked for comment.

The department did not respond to questions about the cost of operating the centers or the number of jobs that will be impacted.

title: RECALLED SOAP
full_story:
A recall affecting nearly 2,700 cases of hand soaps has been categorized as a Class II event by the Food and Drug Administration, according to a recent report from the agency.

The recall, first initiated in June by the St. Louis-based Intercon Chemical Co., concerns six different varieties of soap which were distributed largely to wholesale outlets across 15 states.  An enforcement report published by the FDA indicates all six of the soaps were potentially contaminated with bacteria.

The affected products include specific lots of the following soap varieties, Intercon Foaming Pear Hand Soap With Aloe, in 28.7-ounce containers, Clearly Better by Intercon Foaming Pear Hand Soap With Aloe, in 34-ounce containers, Summit 150 Foaming Hand Soap, in 28.7-ounce containers, Vestis Foaming Hand Soap, Fresh Pear Scent, in 33.8-ounce containers, Laura Lynn Honey Apple Crisp Liquid Hand Soap, in 8-ounce containers, and Laura Lynn Foaming Pear Scent Hand Soap With Moisturizers, 7.5-ounce containers.

More information on the affected soaps, including their lot codes and best-by dates, can be found in the FDA’s enforcement report.

The first two soaps, the Intercon Foaming Pear Hand Soap With Aloe, and the Clearly Better by Intercon Foaming Pear Hand Soap with Aloe, were specifically recalled over possible contamination with several bacterium.  The remaining soaps were merely listed as recalled over “potential bacterial contamination.”

Pseudomonas and Serratia bacteria are often associated with infections acquired in healthcare settings, but they are present in the environment, including in soil and water, researchers say.  Some strains of the bacteria are also showing increased resistance to antibiotics, the Cleveland Clinic and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) note.

The recalled soaps had been shipped to sellers in Illinois, California, Georgia, Iowa, Maryland, Mississippi, Nebraska, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, Washington and Wisconsin.  They were sent to wholesalers and one retail outlet; the FDA’s enforcement report did not identify the sellers.

A representative for Intercon Chemical Co. was not immediately available to share additional details, or provide guidance for customers seeking refunds.
